paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology

Nb–5W–2Mo–1Zr ingots were fabricated from high-purity raw materials (>99.9%) via vacuum electron beam melting
Following the application of an anti-oxidation coating, the ingots were heated to 1350–1400 ◦C for high-temperature forging and subsequently forged into 30 mm-thick slabs.
These slabs were subjected to multi-pass warm rolling at 400–500 ◦C to produce 4 mm-thick sheets.

After pickling to remove surface oxide layers, the sheets underwent three passes of cold rolling (each with a total reduction ratio of 50%) and intermediate heat treatment to obtain 0.5 mm-thick sheets.
